newsitem.title: USA: BPA works with utilities on retail wheeling pilots.
newsitem.headline: BPA works with utilities on retail wheeling pilots.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will work with several Northwest utilities to accomodate their plans to launch retail wheeling projects, but will not establish a policy on its own, a spokesman said Friday.
BPA had previously planned to conduct a formal federal procedure for adopting a retail wheeling policy, but participants in a meeting earlier this week opted for an expedited process, he noted.
Five regional utilities, Puget Sound Power & Light, Washington Water Power Co, Portland General Electric Co, PacifiCorp and Clark Public Utilities, have plans to launch pilot projects.
BPA's cooperation in the planned pilots is necessary because the federal power marketing agency controls much of the region's transmission system.
Sub-group meetings on the retail wheeling policy will be held February 25 and 26, BPA said.
The BPA spokesman also said the agency is unlikely to participate formally in the independent grid operator (IndeGo) being established for the region.
BPA membership in IndeGo will have to be dealt with as part of broader federal legislation on retail wheeling, he noted.
